about: The releases of Orkcraft, newest first: what an installed copy reads to update itself (docs/updates.md). A release marked critical installs by itself when the town opens.

releases.notes: The phone app (a web app over Tailscale, paired from the portrait's menu) shows the questions first, as tiles, the longest waiting first; the buildings at work or in trouble as rows and the quiet ones as marks in a grid, ordered by their roads (a long press lights a building's neighbours); the Task board's to-dos and notes, with + To-do, + Note and + Task written from the phone; Ask, Drop and More in a bar at the foot, and Stop all on a hold so a pocket stops nothing. Away from the town it shows the last town it kept, greyed, and acts on none of it; how many orks wait goes on its icon. It uses the desktop's fonts and both looks, offers itself for the Home Screen, says the version, and finds Tailscale that started after the town without a restart. Orks are called by their orkish names and buildings by what they do in either look: the Test bench's ork is the Mechanic, the UX bench's the Alchemist, and both sit on the Review board at night. Branches & PRs, the Review gate and a codebase Wiki work in their orkspace's project, and a guarded town guards its projects too. The Test bench records a case set's MCP servers once and plays them back after; the Improve buildings sign in to GitHub and send a code change as a pull request with its evidence; the UX bench paints pictures again and lays out a card's parts size by size. In the window: a building's title is no longer cut short, the cards stand on the ground and the selected one in its yard with only its fence lit, the ork at a building's door is drawn as finely and lit as its building, and Town settings always shows the version.

Projects: each orkspace works in a folder of its own (a project), picked when you make it on the War Map — the same folder as now, the town's, a new project with git, or a folder you choose; a folder with no git asks before git starts there. A land's menu has Project… and History…: every change of that map, newest first, and Back to this puts the map back as it was. Before and after an ork works in a project, Orkcraft keeps a snapshot of its files without touching your branch, index or git log, so the History can also take the files back (your current files are saved first). A building's menu has Copy to orkspace…. Build is a tray of small icons by what each building is for, with a new Improve group: the Test bench runs a building's cases beside the bare AI tool and says what to change, and proposals are tried on its copy before they are saved; the UX bench looks at a building's window. A click selects a building, a second click opens it. Cards stand in fenced yards that grow with renown. The Gramophone makes a podcast of two hosts in two voices by default. A phone can be paired from the portrait's menu (a prototype web app over Tailscale). Orkcraft keeps the computer awake while it is open; the screen may still turn off. The Agent pool sorts, plans and judges from its steward's prompt, can work in a folder of code of its own and shows its orks in lanes; External listeners judge mail on the light tier and see who wrote it.

The terminal interface is gone: Orkcraft's window is its one face, and orkcraft tui only says so (Textual is no longer installed). Town Hall → Limits shows what your spend went to over the last 7 days, by purpose and building. A road rule can run on its own model tier, picked in its Edit dialog; a Router rule can name the kind of work it asks for. When a Router, Transformer or other piece of land fails or gets a 👎, the ork of the next building on its road looks at it. The Build list shows buildings first and the land as its own group. Many window fixes: the phone's top bar wraps instead of running off the screen, road labels no longer cover cards, scrolling boxes show that they scroll, Answers shows each whole question, and git errors are said in plain words with what to do.

Settings → AI tools: choose the model each tier (Elder, Warrior, Laborer) runs on, per tool that is on. By default a tier runs on the latest model of its family, shown with its version; you can pick another family, a model the tool lists, or type one. Your choice is kept on this machine and wins over the latest; Reset to latest goes back. The price per million tokens shows when it is known.

Each AI tool now runs on the newest model of its tier's family: agy and Codex are asked once a day which models they have (agy models, codex debug models), so a new Gemini or GPT model is used without an Orkcraft update. When a tool cannot say, Orkcraft names no model and the tool uses its own default. A model you chose by its version in the settings, a building or a task still runs as you wrote it. The tier picker shows the version in use, e.g. Gemini Flash High (3.8). Costs of a model missing from the price table use the nearest version of its family.

When an AI tool fails (not installed, not signed in, a usage limit or overload, no network), the window says which tool and what happened, with Switch to another installed tool (it becomes the main tool and the failed step runs again), Retry, and Details with the tool's own error to copy.

orkcraft started outside a project (for example in your home folder right after installing) no longer stops with "project root not found": the town opens in ~/Orkcraft and says how to open a project's town. orkcraft hooks and feedback outside a project now say what to do.

Your mascot is drawn for your role: eleven heads, each growing its own headgear stage by stage (a keyword tag and rating stars for the ASO gnome, a megaphone and a growth arrow for the marketing one).
Orkcraft updates itself: critical fixes install by themselves when the town opens, other updates are offered.
